memory_candidates.content: In the Logos theory manual (03-dynamics.typ), necessity and the stability modal are both abbreviations of one primitive counterfactual operator (box-arrow) at a Constitutive-Foundation antecedent: box phi := top box-arrow phi (every state verifies top, so the quantifier reaches every world-history), and stably phi := not-bot box-arrow phi (the null state is the UNIQUE verifier of not-bot, so the quantifier collapses to exactly the world-histories agreeing with the evaluation history at the evaluation state -- i.e. BimodalLogic's stab/box-dot). The manual explicitly generalizes this to 'any true sentence whose unique verifier is the null state', naming a true propositional identity as another instance. Open-future/open-past are built by the same point-to-ray agreement-class generalization but are NOT routed through the counterfactual: no Constitutive-Foundation antecedent can express ray-agreement (its event-verifiers are pinned to a single time), so they get their own primitive truth/falsity clauses (def-open-future-past) instead of unfolding from box-arrow.

Before re-applying a prior research report's enumerated contradictions as edits, re-verify them against the CURRENT tree, not just the pinned commit the report cites -- a later task phase may have already fixed exactly what was flagged. Task 872's ledger report (pinned at 4c52993c1) flagged OpenLanguage/README.md as contradicting the tree; task 856's own final phase (phase 15, committed after that pin) already corrected every one of those contradictions, so a naive re-application of the 872 findings as a to-do list would have produced a no-op or a reversion.
